rationale: While initial cohort studies reported normal appearance at birth followed by post-natal progressive microcephaly and leukoencephalopathy presenting around 2 to 4 months of age (distinguishing it postnatally from congenital microcephalies and classical early-onset pontocerebellar hypoplasias), recent fetal genomic studies have identified pathogenic PLAA variants in deceased fetuses with prenatal ultrasound anomalies. Furthermore, expanding clinical reports demonstrate severe structural malformations (such as polymicrogyria, lissencephaly, and cerebellar vermis atrophy), complicating phenotypic discrimination from atypical pontocerebellar hypoplasias and congenital leukoencephalopathies without molecular testing.

evidence.text: Seven patients presented at ages 2 to 4 months with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay, defining a unique leukoencephalopathy with normal initial parameters but postnatally progressive neurological deterioration.

evidence.text: PLAA deficiency causes an infantile epileptic encephalopathy through disrupted ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation and synaptic accumulation of K63-polyubiquitylated proteins, presenting progressive microcephaly across the first year of life.

conflicts: Prenatal presentation: Earlier reports suggested completely normal head size and prenatal development with onset at 2-4 months, but fetal exome sequencing studies detected PLAA variants in fetuses with prenatal ultrasound anomalies.

Neuroradiological overlap: While originally characterized primarily as a leukoencephalopathy with progressive cerebral atrophy and thin corpus callosum, subsequent cases revealed cortical dysplasia (polymicrogyria, lissencephaly) and severe cerebellar vermis atrophy, overlapping with structural pontocerebellar hypoplasias and complex brain malformations.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of PLAA-associated NDMSBA cases exhibit structural anomalies on second- or third-trimester prenatal neurosonography versus truly normal fetal imaging?
new_directions.rationale: Testing whether fetal abnormalities were historically under-ascertained or whether prenatal ultrasound findings reliably rule out classic NDMSBA will clarify prenatal diagnostic specificity.

new_directions.question_text: Can functional assays of K63-polyubiquitin accumulation or cytosolic phospholipase A2 activity reliably differentiate PLAA variants from atypical PCH or lysosomal storage disorders prior to genetic confirmation?
new_directions.rationale: PLAA disrupts ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation rather than classical enzymatic lysosomal storage pathways; evaluating biomarker specificity in fibroblasts or blood could guide clinical triage.
